results.title: Vertices of the spherically homogeneous rooted tree (Kourovka 15.15)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a branching sequence $m \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the vertices of the spherically homogeneous rooted tree are the finite words $(x_0, \dots, x_{k-1})$ of natural numbers with $x_i < m(i)$ for every $i < k$. The length $k$ of a word is its level and its prefixes are its ancestors.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be a homomorphism from a group $G$ to the permutations of the vertices of the tree with branching sequence $m$, and let $v$ be a vertex. The rigid vertex stabilizer of $v$ is the set of $g \in G$ such that $\rho(g)$ fixes every vertex $w$ of which $v$ is not a prefix, that is, every vertex outside the subtree rooted at $v$.

results.title: Rigid stabilizer of a level

results.title: Hoffman–Wielandt inequality for Hermitian matrices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be Hermitian $n \times n$ complex matrices with eigenvalues $\lambda_1 \ge \dots \ge \lambda_n$ and $\mu_1 \ge \dots \ge \mu_n$ respectively, counted with multiplicity. Then $\sum_{i=1}^n (\lambda_i - \mu_i)^2 \le \sum_{i=1}^n \sum_{j=1}^n |A_{ij} - B_{ij}|^2$, that is, the left side is at most the squared Frobenius norm of $A - B$.

results.title: Log-determinant trace inequality

results.title: Sard's theorem on open subsets of finite-dimensional spaces

Then the image under $g$ of the set of points $x \in U$ at which the derivative of $g$ is not surjective has $\mu$-measure zero.

results.title: Hash table with separate chaining
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: For a key type $\alpha$, a value type $\beta$ and a hash function $h : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$, a hash table with hash function $h$ consists of a positive number $m$ of buckets and, for each bucket index $i < m$, a chain stored at bucket $i$: an association list of key–value pairs whose keys are pairwise distinct. The structure itself does not require keys to lie in their hash-selected bucket.

results.title: Empty hash table
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a hash function $h$ and a positive integer $m$, the empty hash table with hash function $h$ has $m$ buckets, each holding the empty chain.

results.title: Hash table lookup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a hash table with hash function $h$ and $m$ buckets, looking up a key $k$ searches only the bucket with index $h(k) \bmod m$: the result is the value bound to $k$ in that bucket's association list, or nothing if $k$ has no binding there.

results.title: Insertion into a hash table
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Inserting a key $k$ with value $v$ into a hash table with $m$ buckets and hash function $h$ keeps the bucket count and every bucket other than bucket $h(k) \bmod m$, and replaces the chain at bucket $h(k) \bmod m$ by that chain with $k$ bound to $v$: any earlier binding of $k$ in that chain is removed and the binding of $k$ to $v$ is added.

results.title: Valid hash table
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A hash table with hash function $h$ and $m$ buckets is valid when every binding lies in its hash-selected bucket: for every bucket index $i < m$ and every key $k$, if $k$ has a binding in bucket $i$, then $h(k) \bmod m = i$.

results.title: Finite map represented by a hash table
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The finite map represented by a hash table with $m$ buckets is built from the list of all bindings of buckets $0, 1, \dots, m - 1$, concatenated in this order: it binds exactly the keys occurring in this list, and binds each such key to the value of its first binding in the list.

results.title: The empty hash table is valid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every hash function $h$ and every positive bucket count $m$, the empty hash table with hash function $h$ and $m$ buckets is valid.

results.title: Lookup in the empty hash table
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every hash function $h$, every positive bucket count $m$ and every key $k$, looking up $k$ in the empty hash table with hash function $h$ and $m$ buckets finds no value.

results.title: The empty hash table represents the empty map
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every hash function $h$ and every positive bucket count $m$, the finite map represented by the empty hash table with hash function $h$ and $m$ buckets is the empty finite map.

results.title: Hash table lookup after insertion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every hash table $T$, every key $k$ and every value $v$, looking up $k$ in the table obtained by inserting $k$ with value $v$ into $T$ returns $v$.

results.title: Insertion does not affect other keys
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every hash table $T$, all keys $k \ne k'$ and every value $v$, looking up $k'$ in the table obtained by inserting $k$ with value $v$ into $T$ gives the same result as looking up $k'$ in $T$, also when $k$ and $k'$ lie in the same bucket.

results.title: Insertion preserves validity of a hash table
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a hash table is valid, then the table obtained from it by inserting a key $k$ with value $v$ (adding a new binding for $k$, or replacing the existing one) is again valid.

results.title: Lookup agrees with the abstraction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every valid hash table $T$ and every key $k$, looking up $k$ in the finite map represented by $T$ gives the same result as looking up $k$ in $T$.

results.summary: The variation-of-constants solution of `z' = P(t) - α z`, `z(0) = z₀`: `z(t) = z₀ e^{-α t} + ∫₀ᵗ e^{-α (t - s)} P(s) ds`. Used for `t ≥ 0`.

results.title: Relaxation solution satisfies its differential equation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The relaxation solves `z' = P - α z` at every time where the (locally integrable) production rate `P` is continuous.

results.title: AND-gate production rate in the logic approximation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: AND-gate production in the logic approximation: rate `β` when `K_x < x` and `K_y < y`, else `0`.

results.title: Single-input production rate in the logic approximation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Single-input production in the logic approximation: rate `β` when `K_x < x`, else `0`.

results.title: Intermediate factor after an ON step
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: `Y` after an ON step of `Sx` from `Y(0) = 0`: `Y(t) = (β_y/α_y)(1 - e^{-α_y t})`.

results.title: ON-step delay of the feed-forward loop
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The ON-step delay `T_on = (1/α_y) log(1 / (1 - K_yz / Y_st))`, `Y_st = β_y/α_y`: the time at which `Y` crosses the activation threshold `K_yz` of `Z`. Meaningful for `0 < K_yz < Y_st`.

results.title: Intermediate factor solves its production–decay equation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `yOn` solves `Y' = β_y - α_y Y` with `Y(0) = 0` (for `α_y ≠ 0`; at `α_y = 0` Lean's `β_y / 0 = 0` makes `yOn` identically `0`, which is not a solution).

results.title: Positivity of the ON delay
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The ON delay is positive.

results.title: Intermediate factor exceeds the threshold exactly after the ON delay
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `Y` exceeds `K_yz` exactly after the ON delay: `K_yz < Y(t) ↔ T_on < t`.

results.title: Feed-forward loop target after an ON step
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The FFL target after an ON step of `Sx` at `t = 0` from `Y(0) = Z(0) = 0`, with `X* = 1` and `K_xz < 1`.

results.title: Simple-regulation target after an ON step
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The simple-regulation target after an ON step of `Sx` at `t = 0` from `Z(0) = 0`.

results.title: ON delay
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The FFL target stays at `0` until `T_on`.

results.title: Delayed rise
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: After `T_on` the FFL target relaxes from `0` towards `β_z/α_z`: `Z(t) = (β_z/α_z)(1 - e^{-α_z (t - T_on)})` (for `α_z > 0`, `K_xz < 1`).

results.title: Simple regulation responds without delay
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Simple regulation responds without delay: `Z(t) = (β_z/α_z)(1 - e^{-α_z t}) > 0` for all `t > 0`.

results.title: Feed-forward loop target after an OFF step
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The FFL target after `Sx` is removed at `t = 0` (`X* = 0`), starting from `Z(0) = z₀`, for an arbitrary trajectory `Y` of the intermediate factor.

results.title: Simple-regulation target after an OFF step
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The simple-regulation target after `Sx` is removed at `t = 0`, from `Z(0) = z₀`.

results.title: No OFF delay
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a nonnegative threshold `K_xz`, whatever `Y` does, the FFL and simple regulation decay identically after an OFF step: `Z(t) = z₀ e^{-α_z t}`.
